title: Suffix-trim and input-echo metering correction for interleaved streaming sessions
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Background: Several customers and internal audits surfaced cases where token tallies diverge from expected counts when streaming sessions are interleaved, hedged, or resumed. Root causes include: client-side input echoes (clients push previous assistant text as part of context), server-side suffix trimming heuristics that differ between pre-tokenization and post-tokenization stages, and partial commits when a stream is hedged or model-switched mid-session. This ticket implements a robust correction path that normalizes inputs before token accounting and provides a tentative-commit / final-commit protocol to avoid double-charging or orphaned credits.
acceptance_criteria: Canonicalize incoming text fragments and metadata to a deterministic pre-tokenization form before any billing decisions are made
Introduce session-level tentative ledger: tentative credits are not billed until final-commit event or timeout-based reconciliation
Ensure resume/reconnect paths (WS reconnect, HTTP chunking) do not re-credit previously billed fragments
Add end-to-end integration tests that simulate interleaved writes, hedged requests, and client echoes with assertions on final billed token counts
Rollout toggle-able opt-in for 1 week on staging and a canary org in prod with metric dashboards for delta between old and new accounting
technical_notes: Normalization rules: trim trailing whitespace, collapse repeated separator tokens, strip echo markers (client-provided echo: prefix), and canonicalize newline sequences prior to tokenizer invocation
Use fragment-level deterministic hashes (SHA256 of canonicalized text + session_id + fragment_seq) to dedupe repeated fragments across retries and reconnects
Tentative ledger kept in Redis with per-session TTL and an append-only journal appended to S3 for auditability

Finalization protocol: on stream close or explicit commit event, mark tentative entries as committed and emit billing events; on timeout/abort, run reconciliation job to either roll back or convert to pro-rated charge per policy

Rate limiter integration: tentative credits should count toward soft quotas to avoid sudden bursts, but hard quota enforcement occurs only on final commit to prevent premature aborts of long-lived streams
implementation_steps: 1) Design canonicalization library and add unit tests (tokenizer invariant tests)
2) Add fragment hashing and dedupe middleware in ingress path
3) Implement tentative ledger primitives (Redis + append-only S3 journal)
4) Wire finalization endpoint and stream close hooks (WS/HTTP) and ensure model-switch path invokes commit/rollback appropriately
5) Update rate limiter to consult tentative counts and track soft quota usage
6) Add integration tests for hedged requests, midstream model switch, and reconnects
7) Deploy feature behind runtime flag and run canary for two weeks, monitor billing delta metrics
8) Roll out to 50% of orgs then 100% if stable
tradeoffs_and_risks: Durability vs latency: writing tentative ledger synchronously increases ingress latency by ~2-5ms; we mitigate by batching and pipelining writes to Redis
Inventory complexity: introducing a two-phase commit increases conceptual complexity for billing pipeline; we will mitigate by keeping audit journal and a reconciliation operator
Storage cost: append-only journal increases S3 footprint for high-volume customers; mitigated via compression and retention policy (30d hot, 365d cold)
Edge-case risk: very long-lived streams may keep tentative credits alive for longer; TTLs and periodic checkpointing alleviate unbounded hold
observability_and_metrics: alerts: >0.5% discrepancy in billed tokens vs expected baseline for canary org
test_plan: Unit tests for canonicalizer (100+ cases including unicode normalization and CRLF/LF variants)
Integration tests simulating: client echo, midstream model switch, hedged requests (N=2), reconnects with overlapping fragments
Chaos test: kill stream sidecar during commit and assert reconciliation fixes ledger without double-charge
Load test: validate Redis-backed tentative ledger holds up at 50k concurrent streams with <10ms p99 ingress overhead
rollout_plan: Canary: opt-in by 3 customer orgs for 2 weeks, daily billing delta review
Gradual: 10%, 50%, 100% over 2 weeks with rollback playbook
Post-rollout: run reconciliation sweep across prior 48h to surface mismatches

notes: This ticket aims to reduce customer-reported billing drift for streaming workloads by establishing a deterministic pre-billing canonicalization and a two-phase tentative/commit ledger. The solution favors correctness for high-impact customers while keeping a path to tune latency tradeoffs after canary validation.
